summary: electro-session ships obfuscated browser/Electron credential and cookie stealer
details: electro-session@0.1.4 is advertised as a 'Session utilities' library but its sole distributed file dist/index.js (referenced as both the package 'main' and 'bin') is a ~1.1 MB obfuscator.io-obfuscated blob whose decoded string array contains browser/Electron credential-store artifacts including 'passwordsPath', 'cookiesPath', 'encryptionKeyPath', 'expires_chrome', 'exported_at', 'uploadedKey', along with references to 'chrome', 'Electron' and 'keychain'. The package pulls in @vercel/blob as a runtime dependency, which provides the network upload channel. Because dist/index.js is wired as both main and bin, the top-level self-defending IIFE executes on any require() of the module or invocation of the CLI, reading installer-owned Chrome/Electron password, cookie, and encryption-key stores and uploading them to Vercel Blob storage controlled by the publisher. The declared 'Session utilities' purpose does not require or justify reading browser credential databases, and the whole entrypoint is wrapped in obfuscator.io output (rotated string array _0x34cb with 4344 entries, decoder _0x5345, hex-escaped strings, self-defending wrapper, control-flow flattening) with javascript-obfuscator declared as a devDependency, hiding the credential reads and the exfil destination from casual review and URL scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
